_comment: 4kwallpapers.com, described 2026-10-12 from the site as it answers today.
robots.txt for User-agent *: Allow / and Disallow /cdn-cgi/ /search/ /recent/ /thumbs/ /thumbs_2t/.
So: no text query (ask=false) - the site's own search is /search/?q=..., which returns 200, i.e. that rule is about it.
Browse by category instead: /nature/ and /nature/?page=2 are plain listing pages and both 200. ?page=1 answers 301,
which is why the page parameter is {nextpage} - empty on the first page, so it is not sent at all.
The two /thumbs/ rules are read literally, which is what robots.txt means: a Disallow path is a prefix of the URL path.
So '/thumbs/' covers https://site/thumbs/... and NOT https://site/images/walls/thumbs/... . The listing page itself puts
/images/walls/thumbs/.jpg in every visitor's - measured 2026-10-13: 200, 31 KB, image/jpeg, and thumbs_2t
is the site's own 800w pair at 99 KB. The card reads that url off the listing rather than building
it: the extension is the wallpaper's own, not a constant - measured 2026-10-13 on /nature/, 23 of 24
thumbs are .jpg and 'Mountain Landscape Wallpaper' (26973) is .png, so a built .jpg name 404s that
one card forever while its neighbours load. The record's 4th group is that src.
The pictures are at /images/wallpapers/<slug>-<WxH>-<id>.jpg, 35 sizes per wallpaper, and that url is buildable from
the listing's own detail link - measured on 5/5 slugs, 3840x2160 came back 200 at 1.4-4.2 MB. No second request per card.
No api: /wp-json/ is a 404 page and the html has no /api/, fetch(, __NEXT_DATA__ or application/json - hence 'record'.
Served by cloudflare with no X-RateLimit header, so there is no published budget to obey; 3000 ms is our own courtesy.
The 1920x1080 file in that same directory is 444 KB. As a card it cost 24 x 444 KB per page on the same rate-limited
path the originals use - which is how the strip ended up drawing empty frames. The originals are still built from this
table, and only the hero asks for one.
The resolution list is the site's own desktop table as shown on a wallpaper page on 2026-10-12:
1920x1080 Full HD 1080p, 1920x1200 Widescreen HD, 2560x1080 21:9 UltraWide HD, 2560x1440 2K|QHD,
2880x1800 Retina Widescreen, 3440x1440 21:9 UltraWide QHD, 3840x1080 Dual Monitor HD,
3840x2160 4K UHD, 4480x2520 4.5K iMac 2023, 5120x2880 5K. Not every wallpaper carries every rung
(the one measured here had 35 sizes, mostly phone and tablet), so a size that does not exist for a
given card fails at download with the status the site answered - which the card says out loud.
